samples.summary: `durable` omits two of the three terms the design specifies, so the chip can over-promise durability
samples.evidence: `docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md` § What the user sees states: "`durable` is the conjunction of three facts: this tab won the app lock, no `PersistDisabled` event has latched this document off, and the store is not failing its writes", and the table below it maps "IndexedDB unavailable (private browsing)", "Quota exhausted after eviction" and "Store writes failing" to `durable = false`. The implementation computes `durable: !lost` where `lost` is latched only by `DurableLossWatch` on the SDK's `local-changes-dropped` event; nothing observes `WafflebaseDocStore` write failures, the quota-refusal path (`withQuotaRetry` rethrows and `evictOldest` returning false surfaces nowhere), or `PersistDisabled`. `useDurableDocument` gates on `supportsClientKey`, the preference, the scope and the Web Lock, but never on IndexedDB being usable. Consequence: in private browsing or on a full origin the durable client still mounts, the chip renders `Saved to this device` and the `beforeunload`/navigation guards are suppressed, while nothing is on disk — the exact direction the design ("the default is to under-promise") and the code's own comment in `durable-yorkie-provider.tsx` ("Over-reporting durability is the one direction this feature must not fail in") forbid.

samples.summary: `not-saved` tooltip does not name which durability case applies, which the design requires
samples.evidence: `offline-local-persistence.md` § What the user sees gives a six-row table of distinct tooltip reasons (not enabled / second tab on this document / IndexedDB unavailable / document too large / quota exhausted / store writes failing) and states "Because `Not saved` is now a *designed* state rather than the only state … Its tooltip must name which case applies." `tooltipFor` implements only the connected-vs-disconnected split plus the opt-in offer; a user stranded because another tab holds the election, or because the store is refusing writes, is told only that the connection dropped or the server rejected the push.
searchedFor: grep 'another tab'|'too large'|'storage space' in packages/frontend/src/components

samples.summary: Offline-transition toast is dropped entirely on a durable document rather than re-worded, as the design states
samples.evidence: `offline-local-persistence.md` § What the user sees: "Two consequences follow automatically: the `beforeunload` guard is suppressed when `durable`, and the offline-transition toast changes from 'keep this tab open' to 'saved to this device'." In the implementation the toast is driven off `stranded = state === 'not-saved'`, so on a durable document no toast is shown at all (asserted by the new test 'neither warns nor guards the unload'). The guard suppression matches the design; the re-worded toast does not exist, so a user who goes offline on a durable document is told nothing.
searchedFor: grep 'saved to this device' in packages/frontend/src

samples.summary: Design doc claims the recovery path reuses `DocumentCopyService` / `POST /documents/:id/copy`; the code does not
samples.evidence: § Losing work anyway says "we already have the machinery for it in `DocumentCopyService` / `POST /documents/:id/copy`", and § See Also lists "document-copy.md — the copy engine the offline-copy recovery path reuses". `lib/offline-copy-recovery.ts` instead calls `createDocument` plus `applyImportedContent` (and, for notes, a hand-rolled Yorkie client in `writeNote`), never `copyDocument`. The choice is defensible (the source is local bytes, not a server document), but the doc now describes a reuse that does not exist, which is the kind of divergence the design-doc discipline exists to prevent.

samples.summary: Housekeeping runs for every signed-in user regardless of the opt-in, contradicting "users who never opt in pay nothing"
samples.evidence: `offline-local-persistence.md` § Turning it on: "Users who never opt in pay nothing for this feature existing." `OfflineRuntime` is mounted unconditionally by `PrivateRoute` and its effect always constructs a `WafflebaseDocStore` (opening/creating the IndexedDB database), runs `collectStale()` and `listRecoverableWork()` on every session — with no check of `getOfflinePersistenceEnabled()` or `supportsClientKey()`. On a build below `MinClientKeyVersion`, where the design says nothing can be stored at all, the database is still created and swept.

samples.summary: The docKey-segment rule is duplicated instead of reusing the exported `documentKeyOf`
samples.evidence: `wafflebase-doc-store.ts` exports `documentKeyOf(key)` with a comment explaining it lives there precisely because "two copies of the rule is how the guard that matched a lock name against a store key came to be silently false" (and `durable-session.ts` correctly imports it). `offline-copy.ts:52` defines an identical private `documentIdOf`, and `offline-copy-recovery.ts:139` re-implements the same split again inside `describeArchivedDocument`. Separately, `TYPE_PREFIXES` (offline-copy-recovery.ts:124) is an inverse of `buildDocKey` in `app/documents/apply-imported-content.ts:37`, so the type↔prefix mapping now exists in two places that can drift.

samples.summary: Recovery toast does not tell the user which of the three loss reasons occurred
samples.evidence: `offline-local-persistence.md` § Losing work anyway: "The user is then told what happened, in the vocabulary of the three reasons" (`epoch-reanchor`, `document-purged`, `actor-mismatch`). The toast says only "Edits to \"X\" could not be reconciled with the server." The reason is available on the `local-changes-dropped` event (`DurableLossWatch` receives it and discards it) but is never carried into the archive record (`ArchiveRecord` has no reason field), so it cannot be surfaced later.
searchedFor: grep reason in lib/wafflebase-doc-store.ts ArchiveRecord and components/durable-yorkie-provider.tsx

samples.summary: `deleteWorkspace` adds an unconditional document-list fetch even when nothing is stored locally
samples.evidence: `documentIdsIn()` calls `fetchDocuments()` before every workspace deletion regardless of whether offline persistence was ever enabled or whether any local entry exists (`removeMember` at least gates on `isOfflineUser`). A cheap guard on `isOfflineUser`/the preference would keep the "opt-out costs nothing" property the design states.

finding.summary: `durable` omits two of the three terms the design specifies, so the chip can over-promise durability
finding.evidence: `docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md` § What the user sees states: "`durable` is the conjunction of three facts: this tab won the app lock, no `PersistDisabled` event has latched this document off, and the store is not failing its writes", and the table below it maps "IndexedDB unavailable (private browsing)", "Quota exhausted after eviction" and "Store writes failing" to `durable = false`. verdict.reason: Verified against the repository: `durable` is computed as `!lost` in durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:107, and `lost` is set only by `reportLoss`, whose sole non-test caller is the `local-changes-dropped` subscription at durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:160-163. No `PersistDisabled`/`persist-disabled` subscription exists anywhere in packages/, and `WafflebaseDocStore` exposes no failure/health channel — its options (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:104-138) have no failure callback, `withQuotaRetry` (:1071-1087) simply rethrows when `evictOldest` finds nothing to free, and `open()` (:327-401) rejects on an unusable IndexedDB with nobody listening. Eligibility (use-durable-document.ts:126-131) gates on supportsClientKey, the preference, the NonDurableScope, the pdf- prefix and the Web Lock, never on IndexedDB being usable. The design states the required conjunction of three facts (offline-local-persistence.md:373) and maps "IndexedDB unavailable", "Quota exhausted after eviction" and "Store writes failing" to durable=false (:384-387), and the repo's own SyncSignals doc-comment (sync-state.ts:43-46) restates the same three-term contract — so two of the three terms are unimplemented. Consequence is user-facing and matches an unmet acceptance criterion (Goal at :52-53, "the chip tells the truth about durability in every case"): on a full origin or with a failing store the chip renders `Saved to this device` and sync-status.ts:220 -> sync-state.ts:85 drops the state out of `not-saved`, suppressing the loud state that guards unsent work. Two near-misses I checked and rejected as counterexamples: the preference reading as off when localStorage throws (offline-persistence-preference.ts:50-56), which the design explicitly refuses to rely on (:134-138), and the version gate supportsClientKey() (yorkie-capabilities.ts:24,76-82) which currently keeps the feature dark at the 0.7.22 pin but is by design a single dependency bump away (vite.config.ts:408-418), so it guards nothing about this defect.
